quote: I never hit a "rock bottom" and no one would have ever said I had a problem.
You don't need to wait until your life has an obvious rock bottom moment.
There was no rock bottom, just a lot of really low days.
I quit well before "Rock Bottom." I hated how I felt in the morning, but more importantly I hated how often I craved alcohol.
I didn't really have a rock bottom moment, I just got really tired of the endless loop of drinking and hangovers.
I always thought I was high functioning too, but was starting to think 'oh, I'm getting older, recovery is taking longer now', 'it would be better for my health & energy levels to drink less'.
The hangxiety was too much in the end and I was sick of feeling so embarrassed of myself all the time.
I use a fitness watch that tracks my sleep and, without fail, no matter how much or how little I drink, my sleep is always garbage if I drink alcohol that day.
I made no promises to myself or others that I'd never drink again but my anxiety and BP dropped significantly after just two weeks.
Like you I just decided to stop last week, hadn't seriously considered it previously, then I found this sub, and it's transforming my life.
I hate the term alcoholic - I think it prevents people from getting help sooner than they should.
I used to obsess over whether or not I "count" as an "alcoholic", now I don't even sweat that and just accept that it's a net negative for me and that's all that matters!
My drinking wasn't anything spectacular - 3-5 glasses of wine nightly. Everything OK on the outside (job, husband & kids, family & friends, fitness) But...I wasn't ok on the inside.
Let me just say that one of the harder parts of quitting, for me, was what people said: "your not an alcoholic" "you're being dramatic".
That was me - So 'high functioning' for so long - no missed work, no horrible work party drama, competent at my job, keeping a neat house, etc.
There is a lot of gatekeeping, or defining, or whatever you want to call it, about what is rock bottom, or what is alcoholism.
Im using reframe to try and cutback.
When I was in moderation mode, I found it incredibly helpful... I actually was able to reduce from 30 drinks to 12 a week using this app. I stopped drinking fully back in February though.
I did reframe for dry January. It was truly great for me.
trust me, when your thoughts aren't cosumbed by moderation (Schrodingers alcoholic cat), it will be a huge mental relief.
I'm sick of the constant mental conflict of trying to stop or moderate.
Complete abstinence is easier than perfect moderation.
I have tried with Excel and notes but I am too lazy to work on those after a week. A simple app which you put a number and registers in a calendar would be awesome.
I have tried few. Many are confusing if you mess up and need a reset. I already feel bad I dont need to spend 5 to 10 minutes to log it. I dont need community, I know other places to get it.
I personally don't count days; for me, an app I could check into when I'm having an urge that gives me a grounding exercise or breathwork etc would be more helpful.
Being able to insert custom milestones. It would be great for holidays. "First Halloween," "First NYE".

i use the reframe app, and what i really like about it is the way it shows me money saved, calories avoided, and drinks avoided. seeing those numbers going up are really consequential and motivating for me.
I just signed up 2 days ago, on day 3, I really like the science behind it and how much alcohol requires your brain. I find that a big motivator.
Just the habit of checking it every morning and every night helped distract me from cravings.
I like the Daily Pledge, I set a notification first thing in the morning and it's a nice way to start the day for me.
It gives you little dopamine bursts by giving you points when you beat a craving or finish daily tasks and check in with your count.
i use sponsi-ai, for me it feels like im texting a good friend or something that reminds me what im trying to recover for.
I like the drink tracker and the daily tasks...I can't stand the meetings so I yeeted those and soon after the community forums. For me it isn't worth the subscription
Yeah it's seemed helpful so far but idk if I'll stick with the subscription, there's a lot to learn on it but I'm not to into the meetings of community forums either.
I'll second I Am Sober, I have it on Android and I like how it rolls with me, I don't have to enter a sober date every Day 1, unlike Reframe.
the first few times going sober, i did really enjoy learning more about the biology behind addiction but have not found myself accessing that area for a while now.
Same vibes for me, mate, I mean I also don't need some app community.
it is however prohibitively pricey - i got mine heavily discounted.
I know reframe is good but I can't afford to pay for it right now.

I'm currently doing the 7-day free trial (a year is $99) so I want to see if it's worth the investment! It seems to have a lot of great tools but I'm not sure where to start besides daily reflections.
Do not subscribe to Calmio. They will continue to bill you regardless of trying to cancel.
I didn't want to do data sharing on a sobriety focused app, TBH.
i really value not needing an account. All my data should be local. And perhaps pin protected.
I also agree with other posters about forgoing some involved account registration process.
I wanted something without community features or social stuff because I didn't want to think about that part. Just open it, see my days, move on.
Couldn't you just mark this on a calendar, or use the notes app? I mean even keeping a pen and paper journal would do this, right?
More power to you, but I feel like once your registering drinks in app, it's clear you a larger problem.
I did not use an app other than Reddit to stop so I do not have any experience with them.
I used the app reframe. It's free. It tries to teach you why alcohol is so bad for your brain and your body. I was skeptical at first, but it helped me get through a lot

there are quite a few people who like to track their total sober days/wins vs just streaks... it would be useful to offer an option for a user to adjust the counter back the amount of time they relapsed.
I joined Reframe after seeing some of their ads on Instagram. I did a 30 day alcohol free challenge right away... I'm now 130 days without a drink where before I was drinking about 15 drinks a week.
I actually like all the extras with community / tracking. But may not be for everyone. I can always leave the community features / stop tracking when I want.
